> This is going to be a 3 piece set of parts. One will be really simple it is going to be a little cable organizer at the back of my desk to separate the power cables and usb-c cables. The next piece will be a tall vertical xbox + laptop mount to be a larger charging station. It will include a headphone hook + airpod/phone charger. The final piece will be a servo powered arm that will be a moveable phone stand connected via pcb. It will have buttons to control a home + in use state. I know it isn't the craziest project, but I think it will be a fun mechatronics project for beginners!

## Design

### 2026-10-12 – I can't believe we are going to use pcbs AGAIN.

**2.25h**

I can't believe we are going to use pcbs AGAIN.

10/12/26

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/e750d6075c840befb76298cba582de6c7b9ec3000694f233679d028be1388b96.png)

BOOM. Design. I honestly spent a while thinking up this one. I was tempted to do the starter project because I'm not great at CAD. My experience mostly came from moving around standard VEX parts around in an assembly.

At the same time, it was kind of ... lame. I didn't want to copy this AGAIN. Instead, I'm making a very simple, but also a real world project that I really need to use. I was first thinking of a project that I kind of needed right now, but all I came up with were a few parts that I lost on my RC car. Which was fine, but that seemed like a small project without much in it.

Then I landed on this, a project that would aid me in something. I had an xbox that was rarely used, and a laptop that I took to school that just needed to be charged at home. I could also add a charging station for my phone, airpods, and headphones.

Still, a little stale? Yeah, I agree. Then I was watching Iron man with my sister (WHO HAS NEVER SEEN IT B4 SOMEHOW!!! & crazy time right?), I wanted to build an arm (i want a dummy iykyk). But I also really needed something to organize my desk, and then BOOM. Merge them together. The arm will move my phone around whenever I need it.

The plan is to revisit PCBs and create a servo powered arm with atleast 2 degrees of freedom. I'll mount it, build an enclosure for it, and my desk is going to be a PROPER engineering geek's desk.

So, I started on CAD with the easier stuff. I watched a few tutorials on what sketches are and through CAREFUL measurements, I produced this:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/57e122596f5c0c31e9d06ad51ca64e10da757b4274597890f44739a07a15f9db.png)

I'm working on the XBOX mount for airflow and plugging stuff in. The holes are the bottom is airflow + power cord. The others are HDMI + USB.

The T shaped stuff is to actually put the xbox on. There are vents on the side and I wanted to elevate it so air can pass through!

Better view:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/21e809de810cec823ccf0e5263b00228343d6ab7dbc8e1385581aafd8540e05b.png)

Also, note to self, fix the slight offset in the back, I can do better...

WHAT a day...
